title: Characteristics of the Sun
seo_title: Primary 2 Basic Science: Characteristics of the Sun Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 2 Basic Science: Learning About Our Environment
standard_text: The Sun is a star that is the main source of light and heat for the Earth. The Sun's position in the sky changes during the day, which changes the length and direction of shadows; sunlight is needed by living things and must be used safely. (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 2, theme: Learning About Our Environment)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Learning About Our Environment): the Sun as a star, light and heat from the Sun, the Sun's path and shadows, and energy from the Sun. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Sun is a star, a huge ball of very hot gas. It is the closest star to the Earth and gives us light and heat. Plants use sunlight to make food, so the Sun is the source of energy for most living things.

The Sun seems to move across the sky from east to west because the Earth rotates. Shadows are long in the morning and afternoon and shortest at noon, when the Sun is highest. Never look directly at the Sun.

Example

When is your shadow shortest?

The Sun is highest.

Answer: at noon

Example

Morning Sun in the east. Where does your shadow point?

Opposite the Sun

Answer: west

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Sun moves around the Earth.
  • Thinking the Sun is a planet.
  • Looking at the Sun through sunglasses.
